title: Giant Wooden Prints Tell a Family’s Story of Leaving Home
summary: Imagine your grandparents had to run away from their home in the middle of the night, carrying only what they could grab. That really happened to artist Annalise Gratovich’s family. They fled Ukraine during World War II with just a few belongings. Now, Annalise makes giant, life-size prints to tell their story. She carves huge wooden blocks—some take six months to finish! Then she adds hundreds of tiny pieces of colorful paper to bring the pictures to life. Her figures look like nesting dolls, but as tall as a real person. They wear headdresses made of plants and animals, and their clothes are covered in patterns like traditional Ukrainian embroidery. Each figure has a name like “The Healer” or “The Builder,” and they hold special objects—a bird, a musical instrument, or swirling energy. Printing one picture takes a team of four people and a press bigger than a car! Annalise says making these prints helps her feel connected to her family’s past. Her show, Carrying Things From Home, is on view in Santa Fe until June 28. If you’re nearby, go see these amazing woodcuts—they’re like stepping into a magical, story-filled forest.
why_it_matters: Art can help you understand your own family’s history and express difficult experiences in a creative way, showing that even sad stories can become beautiful.

keywords.explanation: Fled means ran away quickly from a dangerous place.
Carves means cuts shapes into wood or other material with a tool.
Nesting dolls are a set of wooden dolls that fit inside each other, getting smaller and smaller.
Headdresses are decorative coverings or ornaments worn on the head, often for ceremonies or as art.
Embroidery is the art of decorating cloth with needle and thread in beautiful patterns.
Woodcuts are prints made from a carved wooden block that is inked and pressed onto paper.

background_read: World War II was a huge war that lasted from 1939 to 1945, involving many countries and forcing millions of families to leave their homes.
Ukraine is a country in Eastern Europe that was invaded during the war, causing many people to flee with only what they could carry.
Santa Fe is a city in New Mexico, USA, famous for its vibrant arts community and many galleries showing local and international artists.
Article_Structure: WHAT: She creates giant, life-size woodcut prints that tell the story of her family fleeing Ukraine during World War II, adding colorful paper details.
WHERE: Her art show 'Carrying Things From Home' is on view in Santa Fe, New Mexico, until June 28.
WHY: She makes these prints to feel connected to her family's past and to share their journey through art.

perspectives.description: Annalise’s work keeps her family’s story alive and shares a piece of Ukrainian culture with a new audience.
Some might find the giant prints confusing or too personal, not connecting with the artist’s own feelings.
It’s a unique way to combine old art techniques like woodcut with modern visual styles to explore memory and identity.
